newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nisseki House shares slump in late Tokyo morning.
newsitem.headline: Nisseki House shares slump in late Tokyo morning.

text.p: Shares in Nisseki House Industry Co Ltd continued to slump in late Tokyo morning trade on Tuesday on recent news that the company has not been able to contact its president since early December.

As of 0158 GMT, the shares were trading at 194 yen, down 56 yen from the Monday close, in a turnover of 976,000. Nisseki House was the biggest percentage loser on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

Traders said sales were prompted by uncertainty over the company's management following news in late December that Nisseki House has not been able to contact president Saburo Horiuchi since December 11.
A company official told Reuters on Tuesday that the company did not know of Horiuchi's whereabouts, but added that this would not affect its management or financing situation.

The company, which makes prefabricated houses, announced on December 30 that it had created a new post of vice president and that the president's son, managing director Yuji Horiuchi, had taken up the post. Saburo Horiuchi has not returned home since December 11, and his family reported his disappearance to the police on December 22.
No reason has been given by his family or the company for his disappearance.
